Object structure and dependencies

The dependency tree of FortiWeb objects that hang off a server policy or a Web Protection Profile, cross-referenced against the endpoint registry, a chosen firmware build and the CLI configuration dump.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage
📍 WhereFortiWeb ADOM → Automation → API → Registry & console → Structure tab (URL /structure/)

What is it?#

Object Structure & Dependencies is a reference page in the API area. It shows how FortiWeb objects depend on each other, starting from a Server Policy or a Web Protection Profile. For each object it also shows whether SATOM's endpoint registry covers it, whether a chosen firmware build serves it, and whether it appears in a captured CLI configuration dump.

The page belongs to the API registry tooling rather than to day-to-day policy work. Use it to understand what a policy clone has to carry and where the API catalog has gaps.

What does it do?#

  • Coverage tiles: In registry (tree nodes whose URN matches a registry endpoint), Fetchable (URN) nodes, Missing from registry and Coverage as a percentage of the fetchable nodes.
  • Dependency Tree: the tree of objects and sub-elements as text, with a Copy button. Show URNs / Hide URNs toggles the REST paths in the tree.
  • Registry Cross-Reference: one row per tree node, with FortiWeb object, URN (REST), In registry? (Missing, the matching endpoint, or grouping for a node without a URN), Serves it?, Served by (a transport badge from the CLI evidence) and Test. A filter box narrows the rows.
  • URNs not covered by the registry: the tree URNs with no registry entry.
  • CLI-only elements (not in the dependency tree): configuration blocks that exist in the CLI dump (show full-configuration) but that no REST endpoint names. When some of them hold configuration, a warning states that a clone of this device would not carry them, because a clone writes over REST.
  • Exporter Function Inventory: the exporter functions behind the tree, their role, and where each is ported (not ported when it is not).
  • Structure Overlay (admin): a JSON overlay that adds, edits, removes or reorders tree nodes without a code change.

The tree deliberately covers only the server-policy and Web Protection Profile dependency subgraph. System, Network, Monitor and Log & Report endpoints are in the registry but not on this page, because no policy depends on them.

The "Serves it?" column#

Choose a build in the Firmware selector to fill this column:

Badge Meaning
served A sweep of this build answered for the endpoint
partial For a line rollup: only some builds of the line served it (hover for the list)
absent on this build The build was asked and does not serve it
could not ask The sweep recorded an error
unmeasured No sweep of this build ever asked about the endpoint
— No firmware chosen, or the node has no URN

Requirements#

  • The endpoint registry is installed (it is part of SATOM).
  • For Serves it?: API sweeps recorded for the firmware build or line you pick. The selector lists the FortiWeb builds and lines in SATOM's API version matrix.
  • For the CLI sections: a captured CLI configuration dump of a FortiWeb. Without one, the card says that no dump has been captured and that this is an absence of evidence, not a finding.

Permissions#

  • Viewing the page needs users.manage (Administrator), the same as its only way in, the API entry at the bottom of the FortiWeb ADOM sidebar. Other users get 403 Forbidden.
  • Structure Overlay (admin) is shown and saved only with users.manage (Administrator). Other users don't see the card, and a direct save returns 403 Forbidden.
  • The Test buttons call other pages' endpoints and inherit their checks. API runs a GET through the API explorer, which needs registry.view. CLI runs a live show <path> and needs the legacy backup permission, which backups.create or backups.restore grants.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: the page itself now needs users.manage, like the menu entry that leads to it; the API test button needs registry.view; and the Firmware selector works again.

How to use#

Read the coverage of the tree#

  1. In the FortiWeb ADOM, click API in the sidebar, then the Structure tab next to API-Registry Explorer.
  2. Read the four tiles, then scan Registry Cross-Reference for Missing rows.
  3. Type in Filter objects by name, URN or section… to find one object.

Check a firmware build#

  1. Choose a version or a line rollup in the Firmware selector. The page reloads with that build; the Apply button next to the selector does the same.
  2. Read Serves it? for the rows you care about.

The choice is part of the address (?scope=<version>, for example ?scope=7.6.4, or a line such as ?scope=7.6), so the view can be bookmarked.

Test one row against a live appliance#

  1. Click API (or CLI in the CLI-only table) in the row's Test column. The Test against a live appliance dialog opens.
  2. Choose the Appliance (FortiWebs you can see), then press API or CLI on the row again. The test is read-only: a GET, or show, never a write.

Edit the overlay (admin)#

  1. Scroll to Structure Overlay (admin).
  2. Enter a JSON object with any of the keys added, edited, removed, order and functions. Do not store secrets here.
  3. Click Save overlay. The flash reads Structure overlay saved.
  4. To return to the built-in tree, click Restore defaults and confirm Reset the structure overlay to the built-in defaults?. Saving an empty overlay clears it too (Structure overlay cleared.).

Configuration#

Overlay key Description Example
added List of {"parent": <path>, "node": {…}}. "" as parent adds a root [{"parent": "", "node": {"label": "My Object", "urn": "cmdb/waf/my-object"}}]
edited Map of node path → fields to change. Editable fields: label, urn, via, section, endpoint {"<node path>": {"label": "New label"}}
removed List of node paths to drop ["web-protection-profile/waiting-room"]
order Map of parent path → ordered list of child keys —
functions added / edited entries for the Exporter Function Inventory (role, ported) —

Unknown keys are dropped. A value that is not a JSON object is refused.

Example#

🧪Example — Is a new object type cloneable on 7.6?

An engineer wants to know whether a profile feature can be cloned between two FortiWebs on the same build. On Structure, they pick that build in Firmware and filter the cross-reference for the feature name. The row shows the URN, In registry? with the endpoint name and Serves it? = served, so that build exposes it over REST. In CLI-only elements, a related block appears in the clone-gap warning with 3 rows. That configuration exists only in the CLI and will be missing on a cloned device.

Result#

  • Viewing changes nothing.
  • Saving or resetting the overlay writes the application setting structure.overlay and an audit entry structure.save with the number of added, edited and removed nodes.

Troubleshooting#

Serves it? shows only — after choosing a firmware#

Possible causes - No firmware is chosen (the selector is on none chosen — CLI evidence unfiltered), or the page was not reloaded.

Solution 1. Choose the build again, or press Apply next to the selector. 2. Alternatively, open /structure/?scope=<version>. Add &urns=1 to keep URNs visible.

Verification - The Firmware selector shows the chosen build, and Serves it? has badges instead of —.

"Invalid overlay: overlay must be a JSON object"#

Possible causes - The text is valid JSON but not an object (for example a list), or it is not valid JSON at all (the message then names the parser error).

Solution 1. Wrap the content in { … } and use the documented keys.

Verification - The flash reads Structure overlay saved., and the overlay card shows the active badge.

The CLI sections are empty#

Possible causes - No CLI configuration dump of a FortiWeb has been captured. - The chosen firmware has no dump. A build never borrows another build's evidence.

Solution 1. Capture a CLI dump from the API hub, then reload. 2. Or remove scope= from the address (the selector's none chosen — CLI evidence unfiltered) to use whichever dump exists.

Verification - The CLI-only card header names the device, version and capture date of the evidence.

Advanced#

Advanced Where the data comes from
  • The tree is a hand-authored dependency map (app/registry/dependencies), not a measurement. It is the same for every build. Only the Serves it? and CLI columns change with the selected firmware.
  • The registry cross-reference reads the pure registry (get_registry_endpoints).
  • CLI-only nodes hang from their own root on purpose: a CLI block has no via edge, and grafting it into the policy subtree would suggest a clone path that the appliance rejects.
  • The clone-gap list is capped at 20 entries on screen. The table below it holds all of them.
#structure#dependency tree#registry coverage#urn#cli coverage#clone gap#overlay#firmware
